At the time TXNM and Troy entered into the Merger Agreement on May 18, 2025, TXNM and Troy TopCo LP (“TopCo”) entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement for 8,000,000 shares of TXNM common stock for $400 million (“Financing Transaction”).

On February 6, 2026, Prosperity Works filed a motion requesting that Joint Applicants show cause why the Financing Transaction was not void and of no effect under 1978 NMSA § 62- 6-12(A)(3)(c) and to address the implications a violation of Section 62-6-12 may have on the pending Merger Application.

On March 11, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued the Order Granting Motion for Order Directing Joint Applicants to Show Cause and also issued the Order Directing Joint Applicants to Show Cause and For Other Relief (“Show Cause Order”).
On June 8, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued the Recommended Decision for Show Cause Proceeding (“Recommended Decision” or “RD”).

On May 8, 2026, the Hearing Examiners adopted a revised procedural schedule for the proceeding considering the Original Application, which was thereafter held in abeyance until further order from the Commission or Hearing Examiners by order issued July 2, 2026.

in_service: Sept. 22, 2025 Arthur O’Donnell New Mexico Public Regulation Commission transmitted via email:
Statement of Interest to Facilitate the Stakeholder Process for Public Service of New Mexico’s 2026 Integrated Resource Plan (Docket No. 25-00022-UT) Dear Mr.
O’Donnell, Public Service of New Mexico (PNM) has expressed interest in selecting Gridworks as the facilitator for the stakeholder process for PNM’s 2026 Integrated Resource Plan (IRP).

Gridworks is honored to have been appointed by the NM PRC to facilitate three separate IRP stakeholder processes in New Mexico between 2023 and 2025.1 The key objectives of the stakeholder process —increasing transparency in resource planning, engaging stakeholders early in the process, and connecting planning with the procurement of new resources —are aligned with Gridworks’ interests and experiences.
In New Mexico, Gridworks completed contracts with PNM and SPS/Xcel Energy in 2023 to serve as the NM PRC-appointed facilitator for each utility’s 2023 IRP.
Gridworks has a current contract with El Paso Electric Company to serve in the same capacity for its 2025 IRP, which we expect will conclude this fall.

in_service: As part of this notice, PNM respectfully requests that the Commission initiate its facilitated stakeholder process beginning on or about December 1, 2025 pursuant to 17.7.3.9(A) NMAC.
PNM last filed its IRP on December 15, 2023 1.

More specifically, 17.7.3.9(A) NMAC requires that, “[a]t least six months prior to filing of its IRP, the utility shall notify the commission, members of the public, the New Mexico attorney general and all parties to its most recent base rate case and most recent IRP case of its intent to file an IRP.” 1 Case No. 23-00409-UT, PNM’s Integrated Resource Plan For The Period 2023-2042 In Compliance With NMAC 17.7.3.8.
Consistent with the IRP Rule, PNM plans to file its 2026 IRP on or before September 1, 2026.

The IRP Rule contemplates a minimum of a six-month stakeholder process, and PNM believes the IRP process would benefit from an additional three months to ensure there is a fully interactive and engaging stakeholder process in developing PNM’s 2026 IRP.
Therefore, PNM would like to begin the Facilitated Stakeholder process on or about December 1, 2025.

Respectfully submitted this 20th of March, 2025.

By taking candidate portfolios from the zonal capacity expansion model and evaluating them within a high-resolution nodal production cost model (utilizing the EnCompass platform across 855 nodes), PNM explicitly tracked operational performance across its transmission network.

Using the results of this nodal modeling analysis to calculate location-specific transmission cost adders, and then feeding those adders back into the zonal model for portfolio re-optimization, ensures that the Most Cost Effective Portfolio (MCEP) accurately reflects the real-world transmission investment.

TRANSMISSION RECOMMENDATIONS FOR FUTURE IRP CYCLES While PNM’s modeling enhancements in the 2026 IRP represent substantial progress, PNM notes in its filing that it faces ongoing limitations in its internal ability to fully model surrounding regional transmission systems and capture the full economic benefits of expanded access to external wholesale trading hubs.

Bringing these planners into the IRP process will enhance PNM’s ability to model surrounding balancing authority areas, quantify market depth, and evaluate import/export capabilities at regional trading hubs. b.

On March 20, 2025, PNM submitted notice of its intent (“Notice”) to file PNM’s 2026 Integrated Resource Plan (“2026 IRP”), beginning December 1, 2025. 1 As part of its Notice, PNM requested that the Commission initiate its facilitated stakeholder process pursuant to 17.7.3.9(A) NMAC on or around December 1, 2025. 3.

In its Notice, PNM also informed the Commission that PNM desired to file its 2026 IRP on or before September 1, 2026, consistent with a continued use of the filing deadline cycle that commenced with PNM’s 2023 IRP under 17.7.8(C)(1) NMAC.
However, the IRP Rule’s staggered filing schedule for PNM’s 2026 IRP is impacted by the initiation date of the facilitated stakeholder process under other rule provisions. 4.
PNM believes the IRP process would benefit from retaining the September 1, 2026 deadline, consistent with the schedule set forth in 17.7.3.8(C)(1) NMAC.

PNM therefore requests that the Commission clarify that the filing deadline should remain September 1, 2026 through the granting of this Motion for an extension of the “not later than” six-month deadline set forth in 17.7.3.9(E) NMAC. 8.

Statement of Interest to Facilitate the Stakeholder Process for Public Service of New Mexico’s 2026 Integrated Resource Plan (Docket No. 25-00022-UT) Dear Mr.
O’Donnell, Public Service of New Mexico (PNM) has expressed interest in selecting Gridworks as the facilitator for the stakeholder process for PNM’s 2026 Integrated Resource Plan (IRP).

Gridworks is honored to have been appointed by the NM PRC to facilitate three separate IRP stakeholder processes in New Mexico between 2023 and 2025.1 The key objectives of the stakeholder process —increasing transparency in resource planning, engaging stakeholders early in the process, and connecting planning with the procurement of new resources —are aligned with Gridworks’ interests and experiences.
In New Mexico, Gridworks completed contracts with PNM and SPS/Xcel Energy in 2023 to serve as the NM PRC-appointed facilitator for each utility’s 2023 IRP.
Gridworks has a current contract with El Paso Electric Company to serve in the same capacity for its 2025 IRP, which we expect will conclude this fall.
As part of this notice, PNM respectfully requests that the Commission initiate its facilitated stakeholder process beginning on or about December 1, 2025 pursuant to 17.7.3.9(A) NMAC.
PNM last filed its IRP on December 15, 2023 1.

More specifically, 17.7.3.9(A) NMAC requires that, “[a]t least six months prior to filing of its IRP, the utility shall notify the commission, members of the public, the New Mexico attorney general and all parties to its most recent base rate case and most recent IRP case of its intent to file an IRP.” 1 Case No. 23-00409-UT, PNM’s Integrated Resource Plan For The Period 2023-2042 In Compliance With NMAC 17.7.3.8.
Consistent with the IRP Rule, PNM plans to file its 2026 IRP on or before September 1, 2026.

The IRP Rule contemplates a minimum of a six-month stakeholder process, and PNM believes the IRP process would benefit from an additional three months to ensure there is a fully interactive and engaging stakeholder process in developing PNM’s 2026 IRP.
Therefore, PNM would like to begin the Facilitated Stakeholder process on or about December 1, 2025.
WRA commends PNM on conducting a detailed, highly interactive and educational IRP process with stakeholders in 2026, with the support of its facilitator, Gridworks.

Notably, the Company’s cost analysis shows that its proposal to exit the Four Corners Coal Plant in 2031 is forecast to save customers $500 million compared to maintaining participation in the plant through 2038. 3 WRA divides our comments below to focus initially on the stakeholder process and modeling overall.

equipment_maker_model: INTRODUCTION The Interwest Energy Alliance ("Interwest") is a non-profit 501(c)(6) trade association representing the leading renewable energy, transmission, and energy storage developers and manufacturers working in collaboration with environmental non-governmental organizations to promote renewable energy throughout the states of Arizona, Colorado, Nevada, New Mexico, Utah, and Wyoming.

(3) contract terms that deviate from commercially reasonable industry standards in ways that could reduce competitive participation; and (4) the need to model and account for New Mexico's clean energy law and policy objectives throughout the evaluation.

The IM's ability to monitor communications between the Bid Evaluation Team and the Self-Build Team does not, by itself, ensure non-discriminatory treatment in the evaluation model, the financial assumptions applied to self-build versus third-party economics, or the ultimate selection decision.

MODEL CONTRACT TERMS MUST REFLECT COMMERCIALLY REASONABLE INDUSTRY STANDARDS The model PPA and ESA forms provided with the 2026 RFP contain several provisions that deviate from commercially reasonable industry standards in ways that increase bid costs, reduce competitive participation, and ultimately increase costs to New Mexico ratepayers.

Interwest recommends that all model PPA and ESA agreements incorporate a refined Change in Tariff definition that does not unreasonably subject developers to unforeseen and unavoidable tariff changes beyond their control, and that a limited price-adjustment mechanism be permitted for documented tariff cost increases exceeding a de minimis threshold after bid submission.

Interwest also recommends that all model PPA and ESA agreements incorporate a Tax Implementation definition that does not unreasonably subject developers to unforeseen and unavoidable tax policy and implementation changes beyond their control, and that a limited price-adjustment mechanism be permitted for documented tax cost increases exceeding a de minimis threshold after bid submission.
Additionally, Interwest recommends that EPE not model, bid, or offer contracts for any gas resource lives extending beyond 2045, in compliance with the REA's 100% carbon-free mandate.

in_service: This report provides Staff’s statement on whether El Paso Electric Company’s (EPE) 2025 Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) Statement of Need (SoN) and Action Plan comply with the policies and procedures of the IRP rule.

Staff concludes that EPE’s 2025 IRP Statement of Need and Action Plan complies with the policies and procedures of New Mexico’s IRP rule, but presents a limited number of recommendations for the Commission to consider.

EPE’s initial New Mexico Loads and Resources Table 21 below shows that, even after including committed resources such as the Santa Teresa and Carne projects, EPE remains short of its New Mexico capacity needs in every year of the 2026–2035 planning horizon, indicating a persistent requirement for additional firm capacity and/or demand-side resources.
The 2025 IRP is filed under 17.7.3 NMAC, the Efficient Use of Energy Act, and the Renewable Energy Act, and covers a 20-year planning horizon.

It must demonstrate how EPE will: • Meet rapidly growing loads and capacity needs for New Mexico customers. • Comply with New Mexico’s renewable portfolio standard and zero-carbon requirements, including 50 percent renewables by 2030, 80 percent by 2040, and 100 percent zero-carbon by 2045 for New Mexico retail sales. • Maintain reliability and affordability for its customers.

The IRP identifies a capacity need for New Mexico customers of between 254 and 594 MW by 2030 and between 537 and 1,692 MW by the end of the 20-year planning period, depending on load growth projections.

In its Response to Public Comment, EPE states that “EPE is actively pursuing resources selected in previous REA RFPs, including the Carne project and the Santa Teresa project.” The Santa Teresa and Carne projects combined total 280 MW of solar and 665 MW of battery energy storage system (BESS) nameplate capacity, with in-service dates of February and June 2026, respectively.

equipment_maker_model: Stakeholders found it challenging to articulate their desired model runs.
A factor contributing to this challenge was the availability of the base case model results, which were not available until midway through the facilitated stakeholder process.

Modeling run suggestions were submitted through “modeling request forms.” The utility received 25 unique model requests from nine different stakeholders, seven of which were deemed “non-conforming.” Non-conforming requests included analyses that were not supported by the utility’s current modeling tools.

The 18 “conforming” requests fell into the following categories: ●​ Demand-side options (11 requests) ●​ Load growth and electrification (2 requests) ●​ Supply-side options (2 requests) ●​ Transmission and distribution interventions (2 requests) ●​ Cost of carbon analysis (1 request) Stakeholders with similar requests were encouraged to attend special “office hours” to help refine model parameters.
The model did not select transmission solutions under any scenario, hence there was no opportunity for consideration of these technologies.

Recommendations for managing this tension are included in Section III. 6 An April poll of stakeholders indicated that 14 of 17 respondents were in agreement with the direction the stakeholder requested model runs were taking. 7 17.7.3.9 NMAC.

In one instance although the model consistently produced the same initial portfolio, the Evaluation Team questioned whether the results were economically reasonable.
The team pursued the issue through additional review and testing rather than accepting the model output at face value.

SPS aims to make use of the ERAS process to the benefit of customers and, more generally, evaluate resources to continue meeting resource needs identified during the Planning Period covered by the 2023 IRP.
